source: Northern Territory Government, Department of Resources — Field Guide to Pests, Beneficials, Diseases and Disorders of Mangoes (2nd edition), December 2010, ISBN 978-0-7245-7200-7
text:
Lightning injury
Other Disorder
Importance: Lightning may cause injury or the death of trees and
subsequent gaps in the orchard.
Symptoms: Trees are affected in groups, but not necessarily adjacent
to each other. Most trees are usually affected from indirect strikes where
the lightning travels from the ground and upwards through the trees.
Often the bark cracks and dries out. Sometimes there is a line of dead
bark tissue leading from the ground towards the terminal branches.
There may be brown internal discoloration and an exudation of gum.
Affected tissue may have an unusual cooked smell. Fruit may appear
cooked. The surviving trees are more susceptible to insects (such as
longicorn beetle) and secondary wood rot fungi.
Favoured by: Prevalent in the Top End of the Northern Territory. Areas
with underlying laterite seem especially prone to lightning strike.
Distribution: Potentially in all mango growing areas where lightning
occurs.
Similar to: Damage to the tips of shoots with dead or dried leaves may
be confused with redbanded thrips damage or longicorn damage.
Control Strategies: Trees affected by lightning will be weakened and
may deteriorate over a few months and usually do not recover.
caveat: This source is an Australian (Northern Territory) government field guide, not a Cambodia-specific MAFF publication. It is included as a supplementary international reference for visual identification and general pest/disease biology only. Species presence, seasonal timing (the guide's monthly monitoring calendars reflect the NT dry/wet season cycle), and any pesticide or chemical guidance are specific to northern Australia and may not apply directly to Cambodian conditions, seasons, or registered products. This edition of the source itself does not list specific pesticide products or rates (noted as intentionally omitted pending updated registrations), so none are reported here either.
